proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10234 mūtra gives Prakrit mutta, Hindi mūt, Punjabi mūtar and Bshk. mūλ “urine”. The simple t/tr and named lateral forms are supported; additional aspiration or another northern fricative needs local confirmation. Joint survey comparison leaves inheritance versus transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open. Comparative check: Buksa mut “urine” (f_fgdpypslzzy6u). The exact survey spelling and phonetic marks remain untouched. Stress, vowel articulation, release marks and source palatal/sibilant notation were reviewed as local details; the full form and sense support the same family. The link does not settle uncertain transfer within Indo-Aryan.
